threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep asking for a 'tube station' and the locals only direct you to the buses. You’ll soon learn, Dalston is all about that bus life.
Saw a group of kids on the 59 last night trading Polaroid photos like they were currency. Only in Brixton, right? Can't help but love this place.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids using an abandoned U-Bahn station as their skatepark. They were mixing creativity with graffiti, and it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night currywurst stand that also doubles as a small art gallery, showcasing local talents while you chow down.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local if they instinctively know to step over the Muni delays and still get to Dolores Park with a to-go burrito, no sweat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 6 downtown yesterday—three people left a full cart of fresh lavender on the seat. The smell lingered long after they got off. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume all bars have free tapas with drinks—most locals don't expect them anymore. It’s a real treat when it happens!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take a photo of the Sagrada Família every time they pass by, like it’s a brand new surprise.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie when they still think it's cool to wear flip-flops to the farmers' market. Local shoes are definitely wellies or Docs.
Saw a guy on the 35 bus holding a pizza like it was a trophy, bragging about a late-night slice – didn't even notice he had cheese all over his jacket.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of old Turkish men playing backgammon on a rainy Tuesday, while the café across the street was packed with hipsters. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous pop-up libraries in abandoned phone booths. Grab a book, leave one behind—it's like literary recycling!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals know that the taco truck on 24th has the best lengua, but you’ll never find it on Yelp.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy serenade the Muni crowd with a guitar while a rubber chicken danced in his backpack. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume locals are always in the mood for paella, but in Gràcia, you'll find most of us prefer a simple plat de l'horta any day.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the 12pm lunch rush—while locals are already winding down their mid-day meals.
